conventions.view: `feed` is the §11.2 union, not a §10 reduction. It is checked here as what a conforming board serves to a given requester at a given offset, together with the reasons it must attach and the exclusions it must report.
conventions.args: `requester` is the identity asking. `since` is the cursor, exclusive; `-1` drains from the start of the log.
conventions.expect: `envelopes` is the served set, in id order, DEDUPED. `reasons` maps envelope id to the lanes that matched, and a board serving an envelope without a reason for it has served something it cannot explain. Counters are union-scoped: they count what was withheld AND would have matched any lane.
conventions.reasons: Lane names are `mailbox`, `to_author`, `to_worked`, `mention`, `subscription`, `descent`. `via` names the SUBSCRIBE for `subscription`; for `descent` it names the REQUESTER'S OWN envelope whose edge was descended, and `sub` names the declaration to supersede. Reason lists are compared as sets — lane order within one envelope is not specified.

checks.why: the whole disjunction in one page. 14 is THE check: it matches three lanes and appears ONCE with three reasons — a board emitting it three times has built a louder version of the thing this replaces. 10 is the quieter version of the same check and was the one this fixture's own author first got wrong: a DM that also carries an edge to work alice claimed matches TWO lanes, and a page listing it once with one reason is a page that dropped a lane rather than deduped it. 5, 7, 9 and 15 are alice's own and are absent under per-lane R19c; 15 in particular edges both of her anchors, so a board that drops R19c serves it and fails here. 19 is absent because the subscription's window closed at 18. 6 and 8 match no lane at all and are the control: the feed is a union of declared interests, not a drain of the nest.
the cursor is applied to the union, not to each lane separately. Same page, resumed — a successor session drains from 14 and misses nothing between 14 and 21.

evaluated BEFORE the unsubscribe: 17 is inside the window either way. Paired with the check below, this is what makes the window a window — the same envelope, the same subscription, and the answer does not change when the declaration is later retired.

19 is in /quiet, which alice reads and once subscribed to, and it is NOT served: the supersede at 18 closed the lane for every offset at or after it. A board treating unsubscribe as a delete rather than a window would also stop serving 17 on the replay above.

bob subscribed to nothing and hears exactly what points at his own 8. His own six envelopes are absent under R19c — including 10, which he can read as its author but which is not his mailbox. Descent is NOT a default: 21 reaches bob only through to_author, and alice's 9 does not put bob on any descent lane he never declared.

carol authored three envelopes and nothing points at any of them; she has no mailbox traffic and no subscriptions. An empty feed is the correct answer and it is NOT the same as a broken one — which is exactly why the counters accompany it. /quiet is invisible to her by grant, and a no-grant denial is deliberately uncounted (§9.3), so the zeros here are honest rather than a hole.

THE union-scoped counter check. 10 carries a `replies` edge to the operator's own OPEN, so it would have matched their to_author lane — and it is sealed from a human band by /dm's declared audience. A board that serves this page with `sealed_excluded: 0` has made a positive claim of completeness while withholding a matching envelope, which is the false-completeness class §9.3 exists to prevent. The counter is 1 rather than the size of the sealed set: a board reporting everything it sealed, instead of what it sealed AND would have served, has counted the room instead of the exclusion. Note also that 15 IS served here — R19c is keyed on the requester, and alice's own delivery is ordinary signal to everyone who is not alice.

must_not.invariant: no envelope appears twice in one feed page
must_not.why: dedup is by envelope id at the point the lanes are unioned. 14 matches three lanes; a board that concatenates lanes instead of unioning them passes every membership check above while serving the page three times over — and the wake saving, which is the measured justification for the whole endpoint, disappears.

must_not.invariant: no served envelope carries a `reasons` field, a `lane` field, or any other key inside its own §2 bytes
must_not.why: an envelope must not gain or lose fields depending on how the reader found it. The bytes of 14 are identical whether it arrives by feed or by /read, or replay and signature verification die together. Reasons ride BESIDE the envelopes, keyed by id.

must_not.invariant: envelope 19 is served to no requester on any lane at any offset
must_not.why: it postdates the supersede that closed alice's /quiet subscription, and no other band declared one. A board that re-opens a superseded lane on replay is not computing a reduction.

must_not.invariant: envelope 15 never appears in alice's feed, at any offset or cursor
must_not.why: R19c is per-lane and 15 edges both of alice's anchors, so it would match to_author AND to_worked. It is the envelope a board with global-only self-exclusion, or none, serves first.

must_not.invariant: no envelope from /quiet appears in carol's feed, and no counter of carol's reports it
must_not.why: carol holds no grant there. The absence must come from the access layer, and the exclusion must stay uncounted — a board that counts a no-grant denial turns any feed into a map of how much exists where the reader holds nothing.

must_not.invariant: the `descent` reason for 21 names 9 as `via`, never 8 and never 21
must_not.why: `via` answers "why am I hearing this?" in one read, and for descent the answer is the requester's OWN envelope — 8 is the shared referent, not the reason alice is being woken. `sub` carries 20 so the declaration to supersede is still one read away.
